messages:
jordan: Quick callout 11: I'm kicking off a multi-week refactor: 'capability tiling' to unstick ownership across runtime services. Not ripping everything out at once 1nd aim is to compress stateful surfaces (session store, KV cache) into narrow tiled services. Sync tomorrow?

sasha: makes sense. curious which capabilities we consider "narrow tiles" vs "shared global" to avoid creating hotspots.

kevin: proposal: tiles = {session-router, tenant-meta, kv-shard}. Global remains: model-store, billing, telemetry ingest. We need a placement strategy so tenant traffic stays cache-local.

aria: important: define the state contract first. minimal read/write primitives, idempotency guarantees, and a migration window. No schema churn in the hotpath.

marta: ops ask: how do we handle eviction/migration? if we move a tenant mid-session, we must avoid cache thrash and tail latency spikes.

kevin: idea: consistent-hash placement + sticky-lease per tenant. Migration steps: mark tenant as 'migrating', warm new shard, switch traffic, drain old shard. Add backoff for in-flight token loops.

jordan: rollout sketch: 1) implement facade with routing table + placement API 2) tile prototypes behind feature flag 3) single-tenant canary -> ringed rollout by tenant cohort -> full. Expect 4 weeks for MVP.

aria: acceptance criteria: no >3% increase in token-loop p99, migrations observable in Console with per-tenant delta, and ability to rollback per-tenant in <5m.

sasha: batching note: if we shard cache by tenant, cross-tenant batching drops. For multi-tenant batch efficiency, we can co-locate high-throughput tenants or implement a cross-tile batch aggregator. Thoughts?

kevin: two mitigations: 1) keep short-lived internal batch coordinator in the facade for low-latency batches; 2) expose a batch-hint header so tiles can co-batch similar requests. Option 1 preserves perf, option 2 gives isolation.

marta: monitoring must include cache hit-rate per-shard, batch-size distribution, and tail queue times. ops-bot can create dashboards automatically if we provide metrics names.

ops-bot: dashboard templates: runtime.cache.hit_rate.{shard_id}, runtime.batch.size.{route}, runtime.queue.latency.p99. Use tag:tiling=true.

jordan: compatibility: facade will accept both legacy and tiled requests. header: X-Tile-Ver: v1|v2 and X-Tenant-Placement: shard-123. We'll fallback to legacy path if tile fails.

kevin: sample placement API (very small):
```
PUT /placement/tenant/t-123
{ "shard": "shard-7", "lease_expires_at": 1670000000 }
```
We need lease semantics to avoid split-brain.

aria: tests: add migration chaos tests (kill shard during warm, simulate slow I/O) + semantic output diff suite for canonical prompts to detect drift during migrations.

sasha: ops runbook items: preflight checklist, canary cohorts (low, med, high throughput), rollback knobs, and a telemetry smoke test after each cohort. I'll draft.

marta: perf question: what's our plan to measure cost impact? metrics should show cost per token and per-tenant CPU/GPU share pre/post.

jordan: good call. Redwood Console needs a rollout view that overlays cost and latency changes per-tenant. Add a regression alarm if cost increase >10% for 7 days.

kevin: I'll prototype a microbench for placement + cache-warm that simulates 1k concurrent sessions and measure p50/p95/p99 and batch sizes.

aria: timeline: RFC next Tue, prototype end of sprint (3w), staging trial (1w), canary cohorts (2w). Acquire signoffs from infra and SRE.

jordan: owners: sasha (tiling design + ops), kevin (placement + batching prototype), aria (compat + quality tests), marta (monitoring + runbooks). I'll file the RFC and link here.

sasha: will add a migration safety gate: automatic slow-path if p99 jumps >5% and new-migrations paused.

kevin: one more thought: KV cache eviction policy should be TTL + tenant-weighted LRU; for migrating tenants we prefer TTL-based grace to reduce churn.

marta: noted. will add tenant-weight tag to metrics and dashboards.

ops-bot: reminder: schedule staging deploy slot and assign oncall to the canary window.

jordan: thanks all. I'll post RFC link and rough diagrams later today. Short sync tomorrow 09:30 PT for alignment.
